summative_rubric.title: Number Friends — Summative Rubric
summative_rubric.purpose: End-of-unit rubric covering all 8 expectations B1.1-B1.8. Used to score each child against four levels.

rows.expectation_text: read and represent whole numbers up to and including 50, and describe various ways they are used in everyday life

levels.descriptor: Reads numerals to 20 reliably; struggles with words, ten-frames, base-ten rods, or tally marks at scale 50.
Reads numerals and words to 50; reads 1-2 of the alternative forms (ten-frames, rods, tally) with prompts.
Reads numbers to 50 in all 5 forms (numeral, word, ten-frames, base-ten rods, tally marks). Names a real-life number-use.
Reads all forms fluently to 50; spontaneously volunteers a 6th form or describes multiple real-life uses for the same number.

rows.expectation_text: compose and decompose whole numbers up to and including 50, using a variety of tools and strategies, in various contexts

levels.descriptor: Decomposes in tens-and-ones with adult prompting; cannot find alternative decompositions.
Finds tens-and-ones decomposition independently; finds 1-2 alternatives with prompts.
Independently produces 3+ decompositions of a number to 50, including non-tens-and-ones partner pairs. Recomposes correctly.
Produces 5+ decompositions including creative pairs (16+16, 25+7); explains which decomposition is best for a given problem.

rows.expectation_text: compare and order whole numbers up to and including 50, in various contexts

levels.descriptor: Compares numbers to 20 with prompts; reverts to ones-first reasoning at scale 50.
Compares numbers to 50; uses tens-first reasoning with prompts.
Independently uses tens-first reasoning to compare numbers to 50; orders 4+ numbers smallest-to-biggest.
Uses tens-first reasoning fluently; articulates the rule unprompted; orders sets of 5+ numbers including same-tens close pairs.

rows.expectation_text: estimate the number of objects in collections of up to 50, and verify their estimates by counting

levels.descriptor: Guesses without strategy; estimates often more than 15 off at scale 50.
Uses chunk strategy with prompting; estimates within 10 of actual sometimes.
Uses chunk-of-10 strategy independently; estimates within 5 of actual at scale 50.
Uses chunk strategy fluently; estimates within 3 of actual; explains the strategy unprompted.

rows.expectation_text: count to 50 by 1s, 2s, 5s, and 10s, using a variety of tools and strategies

levels.descriptor: Counts by 1s and 2s to 50 starting from 0; cannot skip-count by 5s or 10s.
Counts by 1s, 2s, 5s, 10s starting from 0; struggles with non-multiple starting points.
Counts by 1s, 2s, 5s, 10s to 50 starting from any number including non-multiples.
Skip-counts fluently; volunteers count-back from a number; uses skip-counting in real-life contexts.

rows.expectation_text: use drawings to represent and solve fair-share problems that involve 2 and 4 sharers, respectively, and have remainders of 1 or 2

levels.descriptor: Distributes objects unevenly; cannot articulate fair share.
Shares evenly when totals divide cleanly; freezes on remainder cases.
Shares fairly between 2 and 4 sharers; articulates a remainder plan.
Shares fluently with leftover-of-2 cases; explains why dealing-strategy works for any total.

rows.expectation_text: recognize that one half and two fourths of the same whole are equal, in fair-sharing contexts

levels.descriptor: Recognises halves; does not yet see 1/2 = 2/4 even with overlay demo.
Recognises 1/2 = 2/4 after the half-on-fourths overlay demo.
Recognises 1/2 = 2/4 unprompted; can also see 2/2 = 4/4 = 1 whole.
Generalises to other equivalences (e.g. 1/3 = 2/6); volunteers connections to compose/decompose.

rows.expectation_text: use drawings to compare and order unit fractions representing the individual portions that result when a whole is shared by different numbers of sharers, up to a maximum of 10

levels.descriptor: Says bigger denominator = bigger piece (whole-number rule transferred). Reverses the comparison.
Recognises that more sharers = smaller pieces with overlay demo; flips back to bigger-bottom-bigger-piece without prompting.
Orders unit fractions 1/2 to 1/8 from biggest to smallest pieces correctly; articulates the bigger-bottom-smaller-piece rule.
Generalises to 1/100 (tiny piece); volunteers connections to fair-sharing scenarios with many sharers.

summative_rubric.usage_notes: Apply this rubric to each child's combined evidence: diagnostic tracker (Lesson 1) + L2/L3/L4 formative trackers + summative worksheet (Lesson 5). The level achieved is the LOWEST of the relevant evidence sources for that expectation.

summative_task_script.title: Lesson 5 Summative Task — Fair Shares and Fractions
summative_task_script.purpose: End-of-unit summative assessment. Captures evidence for B1.6 (fair sharing with leftovers), B1.7 (1/2 = 2/4 equivalence), B1.8 (unit fraction comparison) explicitly via the worksheet.
administration_steps: Bring children back to the carpet after the small-group rotations on Day 5.
Hold up the worksheet and walk through the three parts: (1) fair-share scenes, (2) one-half equals two-fourths, (3) unit fraction order.
Distribute one worksheet per child. Allow 15 minutes for completion.
Walk around and record per-child evidence on the Lesson 5 formative tracker.
Collect worksheets and score against the rubric: 9-10/10 = Level 4; 7-8 = Level 3; 5-6 = Level 2; 0-4 = Level 1.
summative_task_script.scoring_guidance: Part 1 (2 fair-share scenes, score out of 4): captures B1.6. Part 2 (one-half equals two-fourths, score out of 3): captures B1.7. Part 3 (unit fraction order, score out of 3): captures B1.8. Total score out of 10. Map to summative rubric: 9-10 = Level 4 Exceeding; 7-8 = Level 3 Achieving; 5-6 = Level 2 Developing; 0-4 = Level 1 Beginning.

evidence_per_expectation.B1.1: Lesson 2 formative tracker — child reads all 5 forms confidently.
evidence_per_expectation.B1.2: Lesson 3 formative tracker — child finds non-tens-ones partner pair. Mid-unit Numerals 0-50 Check-In score.
evidence_per_expectation.B1.3: Lesson 4 formative tracker — child uses tens-first reasoning.
evidence_per_expectation.B1.4: Lesson 1 diagnostic tracker — child uses chunk strategy.
evidence_per_expectation.B1.5: Lesson 1 diagnostic tracker — child counts by 5s and 10s, including from non-multiples.

certificate.achievement_text: For successfully completing the 5-Day Number Friends unit and demonstrating the skills of a Junior Number Friend. Lila and Otto, and Scoot the puppy, congratulate the student and welcome them to the next adventure in numbers.
skills_demonstrated: Estimating a small collection up to 50 using the chunk-of-10 strategy
Counting to 50 by 1s, 2s, 5s, and 10s starting from any number
Reading and representing numbers to 50 in five different forms
Composing and decomposing numbers to 50 in multiple ways
Comparing and ordering numbers to 50 using tens-first reasoning
Sharing fairly between 2 or 4 friends with leftover plans
